Ben,

Attached is Acme's redline of the MSA (Acme_MSA_redline_v2.docx) and a short note from procurement. Two items we need to resolve before we can move to procurement sign-off and the order form:

1) Indemnity for third-party IP claims: our standard position is that the vendor (Redwood) will defend and indemnify for third-party claims alleging infringement caused by the vendor's software or services. We need clarity about model outputs — specifically whether Redwood will accept responsibility for third-party claims that allege infringement based on model-generated content.

2) Defense control vs. right to assume defense: Acme prefers vendor to assume defense (right to defend) for the vendor-delivered components; procurement is pushing for explicit mechanism and evidence list.

We're happy to run a 30-minute call this week to align on positions. If possible, please have your legal team review and provide a short counterproposal focused on: (a) carveouts for customer-provided data/inputs, (b) how model output claims would be handled, and (c) proposed insurance/limitation language.

Thanks,

Hi all — I reviewed Acme's redline and outlined Redwood's proposed middle-ground below. I've also attached a short counter-redline (Redwood_MSA_indemnity_counter_v1.docx) and our insurance summary.

Summary of Redwood position (proposed compromise):
- Scope: Redwood will defend and indemnify Acme for third-party claims of IP infringement to the extent such claims arise from (i) Redwood-delivered software (the inference runtime and integration code), and (ii) models that Redwood supplies and maintains as part of the covered service.
- Carveouts: Redwood will not indemnify for claims arising solely from: (a) Customer-provided content (inputs, prompts, or uploaded datasets), (b) Customer modifications to the Redwood-delivered code, or (c) downstream outputs where the claim is based exclusively on Customer business logic or outputs that are a direct transformation of Customer-supplied copyrighted material.
- Model-output handling: For claims that allege infringement based on model-generated content ("model output claims"), Redwood proposes the following pathway: Redwood will (i) promptly investigate and (ii) if the claim relates to a model Redwood provided without Customer-supplied copyrighted input, Redwood will assume defense and indemnify; if the claim is tied to Customer inputs or training data supplied by Customer, the parties will cooperate and apportion responsibility based on fact.
- Defense control: Redwood requests the right to assume control of the defense for covered claims (with Customer consent not to be unreasonably withheld), subject to Customer's right to participate at its own expense. We will not settle any claim that imposes an obligation on Customer without Customer's written consent.
- Limits & insurance: Redwood proposes a per-claim indemnity cap of $1,000,000 for IP infringement claims tied to model outputs and software, with a general liability/technology errors & omissions insurance schedule reflected in the attached insurance_summary.pdf. We are open to discussing higher caps or insurance-side solutions if Acme requires.
- Evidence & process: Redwood will accept a short evidence list (claim notice, complaint, and any reasonably available supporting documentation). We request a 30-day cure/investigation window where practicable before litigation expenses escalate.

Open items for Acme to consider:
1) Do you have contractual language that would preserve Acme's ability to engage outside counsel to participate actively (not just observe)?
2) Is a mutual escalation (exec-to-exec) step acceptable prior to settlement?
3) Any regulatory or procurement constraints that require us to keep defense-control language out of the agreement?

If Acme is okay in principle with this mix, Ben — I recommend we prepare a short MAP (action-plan.xlsx attached) and aim for a legal-to-legal redline exchange by EOD Friday (Jan 20). Happy to jump on the call Thursday 2:00pm PT.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary and the counter-redline. A few initial points from Acme/legal/procurement: 

1) Right-to-defend: procurement strongly prefers to preserve Acme's right to retain outside counsel and manage defense strategy for high-value claims; can Redwood accept a carve that permits Acme to assume defense if Acme provides notice and pays for outside counsel but still preserves vendor indemnity?
2) Model output carveout: we're concerned the proposed carveouts are broad — Acme's use cases include automated content generation where there may not be a clear line between Customer inputs and model generation. We need a narrower test than "solely from Customer inputs"; for example, a factual assessment step with an independent technical review (neutral third-party or agreed-forum) to determine causation.
3) Evidence: procurement wants a slightly longer hold period for investigation (45 days) and a specified list of documents (complaint, example outputs, relevant prompt history, and engineering logs).

Rajiv (outside counsel) — looping you to confirm if the above is reasonable; we can discuss on the call. Also, we may need DocuSign-ready order form language for procurement to approve the spend bucket once indemnity is resolved.

-Samantha

Thanks everyone — good exchange. Short summary and proposed next steps so procurement and legal teams have a single source of truth: 

Summary of agreed approach (draft):
- Redwood will assume defense & indemnity for third-party IP claims to the extent they arise from Redwood-delivered software and Redwood-provided models, subject to the carveouts identified by Redwood (customer inputs/modifications/OSS).
- For disputes about causation between customer inputs and model outputs, parties will first engage a technical fact-finding step (30 calendar days) — if either party requests, a neutral technical reviewer can be engaged (costs shared) to advise on causation. Acme requested 45 days; Redwood proposed 30 — open for negotiation; we can set 45 days if procurement requires.
- Defense control: Redwood requests primary defense control for covered claims; Acme may retain outside counsel at its own cost and control defense if it provides notice and pays counsel fees, but Redwood's indemnity obligations remain. Any settlement that imposes obligations on the other party requires written consent.
- Limits & insurance: Redwood proposed a $1,000,000 per-claim cap for IP infringement tied to model/software. If Acme needs a higher cap, let's surface requirements so we can check insurance / underwriter options.

Action items & timeline (proposed MAP):
1) Legal-to-legal redline exchange: Kimberly / Redwood will provide a tracked redline of the indemnity section by EOD Jan 20, 2028. (Kim)
2) Acme legal review: Acme legal to comment by Jan 23, 2028. (Samantha / Rajiv)
3) Exec escalation (if needed): mutual exec review by Jan 25.
4) Order form: Ben to provide DocuSign-ready order form draft once indemnity is agreed; target signature within 7–10 business days after final redline. (Ben)
5) Neutral reviewer: If invoked, parties agree to pick from a short list of neutral technical reviewers; costs to be split 50/50.

Call: Confirmed — Thursday Jan 18 at 2:00pm PT (invite to follow).

Links & attachments: DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abcd-1234; HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4591; Action-plan.xlsx attached.

I'll follow up after the legal-to-legal exchange with the MAP updated in the Deal record. Thanks for the partnership — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
